audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL-focused specs including Homestead state transitions, EVM interpreter, control flow opcodes, REVERT instruction, BLAKE2F precompile, deposit contract (EL-CL bridge), eth/68 P2P networking, EIP-7919 RPC verification, EIP-7749 wallet signing, and EIP-7966 synchronous transaction submission.

out_of_scope: Consensus Layer internals beyond deposit processing
Beacon Chain state transitions (not covered in this batch)

execution_layer.threat: Submit malformed transactions, resource exhaustion via synchronous RPC, phishing via signing requests
Eclipse attacks, send invalid blocks/transactions, lie about transaction sizes in announcements, bandwidth exhaustion

execution_layer.entry_point: EVM Execution (CALL to precompiles, JUMP/JUMPI destinations, REVERT abuse)
execution_layer.threat: Gas exhaustion via BLAKE2F rounds, invalid jump destinations, state manipulation via revert patterns
Submit invalid BLS signatures to burn ETH, grief legitimate depositors, deposit spam

consensus_layer.threat: Propose invalid blocks, submit conflicting attestations, censorship

consensus_layer.entry_point: External APIs (MEV-Boost relay, checkpoint sync endpoint, RPC providers)
consensus_layer.threat: Provide incorrect data, censorship, denial of service, false proofs

misclassified_entities.reason: Transaction Execution (EVM) is an internal EL component, not an external entity. It is the execution engine itself producing receipts.
Transaction Executor is the higher-level EL transaction processing pipeline, an internal component that invokes the VM. Not an external entity.
EVM Bytecode is data (contract code), not an external entity that sends data into the system. The bytecode is already stored within the system.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer via P2P (devp2p)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P Network (devp2p) - block propagation, eth/68 NewPooledTransactionHashes
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P peers are unauthenticated. Any node can join the network and submit blocks or transaction announcements. Peers may lie about transaction types/sizes in eth/68 announcements. All data must be fully validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Public RPC endpoint, no authentication required. Users can submit arbitrary transaction data including malformed transactions. Synchronous RPC (EIP-7966) adds resource exhaustion risk via long-held connections.

trusted_external_entities.name: Depositor via Deposit Contract
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Deposit Contract deposit() function via EL transaction
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any entity can call the deposit contract with arbitrary pubkey, signature, and withdrawal credentials. The contract performs only minimal validation (data root check, amount check). BLS signature verification is deferred to the beacon chain. Invalid deposits result in burned ETH.

trusted_external_entities.name: Third-Party RPC Provider
trusted_external_entities.rationale: RPC providers are third-party services that may be compromised or malicious. EIP-7919 explicitly addresses this by requiring cryptographic proofs for all responses. Data must be verified against known state roots.

trusted_external_entities.name: Light Client via RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Light clients query logs without running a full node. They are untrusted consumers of EL data, but the system must serve them correct and complete data with proofs.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp via Wallet JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DApps request signatures from wallets. A malicious DApp could request signatures for fraudulent purposes. The wallet must display the validator address and data for user approval. Domain separation via EIP-191 prefix prevents cross-validator signature reuse.

trusted_external_entities.name: Signature Presenter via Contract Call
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Smart contract function call presenting signature for verification (EIP-7749 validator)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any entity can present a signature to a validator contract for verification. The validator must reconstruct the expected message using its own address, hash it, and recover the signer via ecrecover. Untrusted input.

trusted_external_entities.name: Contract Caller via CALL to Precompile
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any contract can invoke the BLAKE2F precompile with arbitrary input. The precompile must validate exact 213-byte input length and valid final flag (0 or 1). Gas is charged dynamically based on rounds parameter, preventing resource exhaustion.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer via P2P
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P Network - block submission with PoW (Homestead) or PoS proposal
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Miners/validators produce blocks that must be fully validated: header, ommers, transactions, state roots, PoW difficulty target. A malicious miner could submit blocks with invalid PoW, incorrect difficulty, or manipulated timestamps.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Block Validation Pipeline (validate_header, validate_ommers, apply_body, verify_roots)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full block validation required: header fields, gas limit bounds, PoW/PoS validity, transaction execution correctness, state root verification. All data from peers is potentially malicious.

Peers may lie about transaction types and sizes. Node must validate array length consistency (types, sizes, hashes same length), apply throttling policies based on announced sizes, and verify actual transaction data after fetch.

Full transaction validation required. Timeout parameter must be bounded by node-configured maximum to prevent resource exhaustion. Node must handle concurrent synchronous connections without blocking consensus operations.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Transaction Validation (check_transaction: gas, nonce, balance, EOA)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: All transaction fields must be validated: sufficient gas available in block, exact nonce match, sender balance covers gas*price + value, sender is EOA. Invalid transactions must be rejected.

Contract validates deposit_data_root integrity, minimum deposit amount, and parameter lengths (pubkey=48, withdrawal_credentials=32, signature=96 bytes). BLS signature verification is NOT performed at this boundary - it is deferred to CL. Invalid BLS signatures result in burned ETH.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Beacon Chain Deposit Processing (via Eth1Data voting)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: CL must perform full BLS12-381 signature verification on all deposits read from the deposit contract. Invalid signatures must be silently ignored without affecting chain state. The progressive Merkle tree root must be verified.

All RPC responses must include cryptographic proofs (Merkle proofs against known state roots). Proofs must be verified for both correctness and completeness. Providers with invalid proofs must be flagged as malicious.
Query results must include completeness proofs. The 2D log index must provide bounded false-positive guarantees. System must handle potentially expensive queries without DoS.

Wallet must display validator address and data to user for approval before signing. Message must be prefixed with 0x19 || 0x00 || validatorAddress to ensure domain separation. Signature cannot be replayed across different validators or as a transaction.

Validator must reconstruct message using its own address (not a supplied address), compute keccak256 hash, and use ecrecover to verify the signer. Must not accept signatures intended for other validators.

Input must be exactly 213 bytes. Final flag must be 0 or 1. Gas cost is rounds * GAS_BLAKE2_PER_ROUND, preventing resource exhaustion for high round counts. Invalid inputs must raise InvalidParameter exception.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Block Header Validation and PoW Verification
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full header validation: parent hash, gas limit within parent +/- 1/1024 and >= 5000, timestamp, difficulty per formula with bomb. PoW: hashimoto_light verification, mix_digest match, result <= MAX_VALUE/difficulty. Max 2 ommers, age 1-6 blocks.
